page.layout: One printed page, left, page 286, with running head "De Ecclesia" at the top and one column of text, which runs over the foot to the next page. Right of it, a second printed page is cut off at the right edge of the scan. Only the first letters of its lines are visible, so it is transcribed as a fragment. No margin notes, no headings, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.l: praeter illos sese in Ecclesiae ministerio intru-
serint, vocationem in Ecclesia nullam proba-
re possunt. Ac proinde Iesuitae, omnesque re-
liqui regularium ordines, non dico successio-
nem ab Apostolis, sed ne vocationem quidem
suam demonstrare possunt.
Itaque Episcopos, & presbyteros, quamuis
in nonnullis religionis capitibus à nobis dis-
sentiant, tamen non solum ferendos, verum
propter loci, quem occupant, dignitatem,
& successionem ab Apostolis, venerabiles
aesti-mamus: de quibus spes est, ipsos propter eru-
ditionem & iudicium, quo inter eos plurimi
excellunt, praestigias Iesuiticas tandem ali-
quando perspectas atque exploratas abomi-
natūros, veritatem quoque nobiscum amplexatu-
ros. Maxime vero venerabilibus Episcopis, &
clero Gallicano hanc mentis sanitatem ex-
optamus, & precibus à Deo Opt.Max. exopta-
mus, apud quos Concilii Tridentini
decreta authoritatem obtinere nunquam potuerunt.
Et profecto, qui inter eos eruditione & vitae
sanctimonia praestant, facile perspiciunt, quo
tendat Iesuitarum furiosus in Ecclesia impe-
tus: nempe non ad aedificationem, sed ad fidei
destructionem, ad Ecclesiae horrendam con-
turbationem, ad Regum perniciem, & Re-
rumpublicarum ruinam. Si in Galliis,
Germa-
nia, Hispania, Italia, cum Ecclesiae statum vi-
dere liceret, qui ante fraterculorum exortos
Ordines in istis nationibus florere solebat,
Ecclesiam omnino perditam non possemus

page.notes: The right-hand printed page is cut off at the scan edge. Only the first letters of its lines are visible. The fragment paragraph is a transcription of those letters, not of words. Several are doubtful and are not marked individually. The left-hand page has long s printed as s, which is written as plain s. The line "Iesuiticas" and similar readings are as printed. Printed hyphens at line ends are kept. The text ends mid-word at "deplo-" and continues on the next page.
